resources.string: Why did my stream stutter?

Active samples: %1$d. Evidence covers the last 30 seconds. Several stages can be slow at once; these observations suggest causes, not a guaranteed diagnosis. No video or personal information is recorded.
Not enough recent video to assess. Play for a few seconds with the menu closed, then return just after a stutter.
No repeated bottleneck was observed in the available measurements. Short spikes and unmeasured stages can still cause a stutter.
Network: repeated frame loss or round-trip variation. Try a lower bitrate, a wired PC or a less congested Wi-Fi connection.
Decode: output repeatedly took at least one frame interval. Try a lower resolution or frame rate; lowering bitrate alone may not help.

Host: the PC\'s slower frames took longer than the frame interval. When the PC sends timing reports, this time runs from the frame to its last packet sent, so it includes waiting and sending, not only encoding. Compare game/GPU load and a lower game frame limit.
Presentation: frames were released faster than they were shown, and reached the screen late. Compare frame-pacing modes and the screen refresh rate.
Temperature: Android reported high thermal pressure. Lower frame rate/resolution or disable expensive client processing; allow the device to cool.

Largest observed values:
Frame loss: %1$s %%
Decode: %2$s ms
Host processing p95: %3$s ms
Display wait p95: %4$s ms
These stages do not add up to input-to-screen latency.

These stages do not add up to input-to-screen latency.
The PC did not report its current encoder bitrate. The trial was not applied.
The PC’s bitrate has changed since the trial. Undo was cancelled to preserve that change.
The encoder is already at the minimum trial bitrate. No change was made.

Repeating stalls: %2$d network stalls in the last 20 minutes started about every %1$s. A steady rhythm like this usually comes from background Wi-Fi scans on this device or on the PC. To reduce them:
• Android: Settings → Location → Location services, turn off Wi-Fi scanning and Bluetooth scanning.
• Android: leave Developer options → Wi-Fi scan throttling on.
• Close apps that look for networks or nearby devices while streaming.
• PC: connect it by cable, or stop tools that scan for Wi-Fi networks.
Nightjar already holds Android’s low-latency Wi-Fi lock while streaming, which asks the system to delay scans; some devices scan anyway.

Bursts: in %1$d of the last %2$d seconds, frames arrived bunched together, several at once. When the PC sends timing reports, they show no delay on its side that explains this. A cable or a less busy 5 or 6 GHz Wi-Fi channel may help.

Nothing repeated in the last 30 seconds. A single short spike can still cause a stutter now and then.
Your Wi-Fi or network delivers frames in uneven bursts or loses some, which causes brief stutters. A slightly lower bitrate usually smooths this out.
The PC sent finished frames late, so they reached this device unevenly. Closing other work on the PC or a slightly lower bitrate usually helps.
Your PC’s GPU or encoder fell behind the game’s frame rate. A lower stream resolution takes load off the PC.
This device’s video decoder took longer than one frame to finish a picture. A lower stream resolution or frame rate keeps motion smooth.
Frames arrived and were decoded in time, but the screen showed them late. Another frame pacing mode or the screen’s refresh rate usually fixes this.
This device capped the network receive buffer below what high-bitrate video needs, so bursts of packets were dropped. A slightly lower bitrate stops the loss.
